newsitem.title: ITALY: EU's Monti calls for Italy banking restructuring.
newsitem.headline: EU's Monti calls for Italy banking restructuring.

text.p: European Commissioner Mario Monti has called for an urgent restructuring of Italy's banking system ahead of European economic and monetary union scheduled to start at the beginning of 1999.
Italian newspapers reported his remarks on Sunday from a seminar held at Cernobbio on the shores of Lake Como, north of Milan.
"If it (Italy) wants to compete it is necessary to make an effort to restructure its banking system," financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported Monti telling his audience at the seminar.
His remarks echo a number of commentators and analysts who say Italy's banking system is fragmented, inefficient, over-staffed and produces a low return on equity invested.

"It is very difficult for an economy to be able to compete internationally without an efficient banking system. Above all ahead of the introduction of the euro," Corriere della Sera reported Monti saying.

The governor of the Bank of Italy Antonio Fazio has warned over the banking system's low profitability and its need for restructuring. He has has urged banks to cut their workforces by around 30,000, or nearly 10 percent, from their current 330,000 staffing level.

Italy has nearly 1,000 different banking groups, with many controlled by the state or charity foundations and the banking industry has been slow to restructure along the lines of the banking industries in Britain and the U.S.

La Repubblica newspaper illustrated the high level of staffing by producing figures based at the end-September 1996, which showed Banca di Roma had 22,207 employees with some 1,246 branches, Italy's largest bank San Paolo di Torino had 20,702 staff with 1,227 branches while state-controlled BNL has 20,050 with 636 branches.
